title: Pre-contact Muisca ritual offering activity at Lake Guatavita
summary: Archaeological and ethnohistorical evidence supports Lake Guatavita as a Muisca ritual shrine where offerings occurred before European contact. A 2009 archaeological survey, published in Latin American Antiquity, supports small-scale ritual offering activity rather than the conspicuous mass investiture spectacle described in later colonial accounts. The latter remains a separately modeled disputed historical interpretation.

time.note: Pre-European-contact Muisca period; the surviving evidence does not establish one discrete ceremony date.

historicity.note: Confidence refers to ritual shrine/offering activity, not to every detail of later colonial investiture narratives.

uncertainty: The archaeology supports ritual use and offerings but does not establish a single lavish investiture ceremony matching later colonial descriptions.
The Pasca raft is contextual evidence for Muisca votive imagery, not an artifact recovered from Lake Guatavita.
Exact dates, frequency, scale, and participants of individual pre-contact ceremonies remain uncertain.
alternative_interpretations: Colonial chroniclers may have amplified or conflated different Muisca offering traditions into a more spectacular investiture narrative.
The El Dorado narrative may reflect multiple transmission and expansion processes rather than a single-event origin.

review.note: Canonical scope is limited to the archaeologically defensible shrine/offering activity; grand investiture details remain disputed claims.
